rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3 and 3.2, Tables 1-3 <U+2013> the authors fabricated the solar-powered applicator and measured dripper/sprinkler discharge, solar insolation and panel/battery voltage at CCSHAU Hisar, and evaluated it in a bottle gourd crop. Q2: Section 3.2 and Abstract <U+2013> average dripper and sprinkler discharge of 79.9 and 640.2 ml/min under average insolation of about 948 W/m2 (Tables 2, 3), and the machine with drip was evaluated in bottle gourd and reported as satisfactory for saving the crop under dry-spell conditions. Q9: Table 2 reports discharge as 79.9 <U+00B1> 6.85 and 640.2 <U+00B1> 18.33 ml/min (mean <U+00B1> SD over 10 tests); Table 3 reports insolation 947.86 <U+00B1> 124.3 W/m2 and voltages with SD.
rows.notes: The quantitative results concern only machine performance (discharge, insolation, voltage). The crop-rescue effect itself is a single unquantified statement that performance in bottle gourd was 'satisfactory to save the crop'; no soil moisture, crop survival or yield data, no control, one site, one crop, one season. Tables 2 and 3 are sourced from the institute's commercial test report (Anonymous 2019) by the same testing centre. The SD in Q9 applies to discharge/insolation numbers cited in the passage, not to the crop-rescue outcome. No conditions or limitations stated from own findings.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3 and 3.2, Tables 2-3 <U+2013> own measurements of discharge rate, insolation and voltage of the fabricated applicator.
rows.notes: The study reports no measurement of water use, water saving or water-use efficiency of its own. Water-saving figures (30-70% for drip, 35% for sprinkler) and the 85% application efficiency are cited from literature or asserted in the introduction/materials sections, not measured. Only discharge rates of the emitters and the machine's electrical performance were recorded.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3 and 3.2, Tables 2-3 <U+2013> own measurements of discharge rate, insolation and voltage of the fabricated applicator.
rows.notes: No crop production, yield, growth or survival data are reported. The only crop-related statement is that the machine's performance in bottle gourd was 'satisfactory to save the crop under dry spell conditions', with no measurements or comparison; statements about increased yield and 'more crop per drop' are introductory assertions or expectations, not own results on crop production.

notes: Short machine-development paper (7 pages). Own data are limited to emitter discharge rates, solar insolation and panel/battery voltages (Tables 2-3, from the institute's test report); crop evaluation in bottle gourd is reported only qualitatively. Note inconsistency in test date (abstract says January 2019, Section 3.2 says January 2018).
